source.text: שִׁ֥יר הַֽמַּעֲל֗וֹת לְדָ֫וִ֥דלוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה שֶׁהָ֣יָה לָ֑נוּ יֹֽאמַר־נָ֝א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents, of David. If not YHWH who was for us — let say, please, Israel —

en.L: A song of ascents. Of David. If [it had] not [been] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who was for us — let Israel now say —
en.B: A song of ascents. Of David. Let Israel say it now: if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not stood with us,
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. By David. Let Israel say it: What if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not been on our side?

fr.L: Cantique des montées. De David. Si [ce n’avait] pas [été] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui était pour nous — qu’Israël le dise donc —
fr.B: Cantique des montées. De David. Qu’Israël le dise maintenant : si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne s’était pas tenu avec nous,
fr.R: Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem. De David. Qu’Israël le dise : Que serait-il arrivé si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’avait pas été de notre côté ?

sw.L: Wimbo wa kupanda. Wa Daudi. Kama [isingekuwa] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyekuwa upande wetu — Israeli na aseme sasa —
sw.B: Wimbo wa kupanda. Wa Daudi. Israeli na aseme sasa: kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asingesimama pamoja nasi,
sw.R: Wimbo wa safari ya kupanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Wa Daudi. Israeli na aseme: Ingekuwaje kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asingekuwa upande wetu?

es.L: Cántico de las subidas. De David. Si no [hubiera sido] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien estaba a favor nuestro —que lo diga ahora Israel—,
es.B: Cántico de las subidas. De David. Que lo diga ahora Israel: si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hubiera estado con nosotros,
es.R: Canto para el viaje de subida a Jerusalén. De David. Que lo diga Israel: ¿Qué habría pasado si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hubiera estado de nuestro lado?

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: As in 120:1, the short title and the first line are counted together as verse 1, so the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
decisions.reason: As in 120:1: one of the fifteen songs probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: of David: linked with David
decisions.reason: Four of the Songs of Ascents (122, 124, 131, 133) add "of David", and one (127) "of Solomon". As elsewhere in the Psalms, "of" may mean the psalm is by him, belongs to a collection named for him, or is written for or about him. Some ancient copies of these titles lack the name.

decisions.choice: if not ... for us: what would have happened
decisions.reason: "If not" (lule) introduces something that did not happen: the LORD was on Israel's side. The sentence is broken off by "let Israel say", begun again in verse 2, and finished with "then" in verses 3-5.

decisions.choice: let Israel say: the people join in
decisions.reason: The leader calls on the whole people to repeat the words, as in 118:2 and 129:1.

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 120:1.

decisions.choice: Let Israel say it now: first
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the call to Israel first so that the record can end with the unfinished sentence; Literal keeps the Hebrew order.

source.text: לוּלֵ֣י יְ֭הוָה שֶׁהָ֣יָה לָ֑נוּ בְּק֖וּם עָלֵ֣ינוּ אָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: If not YHWH who was for us, when rose up against us a man,

en.L: if [it had] not [been] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} who was for us when {{gender:people|men}} rose up against us,
en.B: if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not stood with us when {{gender:people|men}} rose up against us,
en.R: What if {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had not been on our side when {{gender:people|men}} attacked us?

fr.L: si [ce n’avait] pas [été] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} qui était pour nous, quand des {{gender:humains|hommes}} se sont levés contre nous,
fr.B: si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne s’était pas tenu avec nous quand des {{gender:humains|hommes}} se sont levés contre nous,
fr.R: Que serait-il arrivé si {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} n’avait pas été de notre côté quand des {{gender:humains|hommes}} nous ont attaqués ?

sw.L: kama [isingekuwa] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliyekuwa upande wetu, watu walipoinuka dhidi yetu,
sw.B: kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asingesimama pamoja nasi watu walipotuinukia,
sw.R: Ingekuwaje kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asingekuwa upande wetu watu walipotushambulia?

es.L: si no [hubiera sido] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quien estaba a favor nuestro cuando se alzaron contra nosotros {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}},
es.B: si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hubiera estado con nosotros cuando {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} se levantaron contra nosotros,
es.R: ¿Qué habría pasado si {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no hubiera estado de nuestro lado cuando {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} nos atacaron?

decisions.choice: a man: mere humans
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) means human beings. The enemies are only human, set against the LORD who was on Israel's side.

decisions.choice: the opening repeated
decisions.reason: Verse 2 repeats the opening of verse 1 and adds when the danger came; the sentence runs on into verse 3.

decisions.choice: people
decisions.reason: The word means human beings in general; the gender setting gives the traditional "men".

decisions.choice: "humains" by default, "hommes" as the gender alternative, on the noun for ʾadam
decisions.reason: ʾAdam means human beings, mere mortals set against God. As the French terms settle, the gender setting goes on the noun: "humains" by default, the traditional "hommes" as the alternative.

decisions.choice: "watu" (people) with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adam means human beings, and Swahili "watu" says that plainly. The only other wording, "wanaume", would mean males only and change the sense, so Swahili has no setting here where the English has one.

decisions.choice: a gender setting on "los seres humanos" (L), "las personas" (B, R), with "los hombres" as the other wording
decisions.reason: The Hebrew 'adam means human beings. Spanish has the same choice the English setting offers, so the setting stands here; the plural keeps the verb the same in both wordings.

source.text: אֲ֭זַי חַיִּ֣ים בְּלָע֑וּנוּ בַּחֲר֖וֹת אַפָּ֣ם בָּֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: then alive they would have swallowed us, when burned their anger against us,

en.L: then they would have swallowed us alive, when their anger burned against us,
en.B: then they would have devoured us alive in the heat of their anger against us,
en.R: Then they would have eaten us alive, because their anger burned against us.

fr.L: alors ils nous auraient engloutis vivants, quand leur colère s’est enflammée contre nous,
fr.B: alors ils nous auraient dévorés vivants dans le feu de leur colère contre nous,
fr.R: Alors ils nous auraient mangés vivants, parce que leur colère brûlait contre nous.

sw.L: basi wangetumeza tukiwa hai, hasira yao ilipowaka juu yetu,
sw.B: basi wangetumeza wazima katika ukali wa hasira yao dhidi yetu,
sw.R: Wangetumeza tukiwa hai, kwa sababu walitukasirikia mno.

es.L: entonces nos habrían tragado vivos, cuando su ira ardía contra nosotros;
es.B: entonces nos habrían devorado vivos en el calor de su ira contra nosotros;
es.R: Entonces nos habrían comido vivos, porque su enojo ardía contra nosotros.

decisions.choice: swallowed alive: like the grave
decisions.reason: To be swallowed alive is what the grave does (Proverbs 1:12); the earth swallowed Korah and his followers alive (Numbers 16:30-33). The enemies are pictured as a monster or as death itself.

decisions.choice: then: what would have happened
decisions.reason: "Then" (azay) begins each of verses 3-5, saying what would have happened if the LORD had not been with Israel.

decisions.choice: their anger burned: they were furious
decisions.reason: Anger is often said to burn or flare up (2:12; 106:40).

records.literal_gloss: then the waters would have overflowed us, a torrent would have passed over our soul,

en.L: then the waters would have swept over us, a torrent would have passed over our soul,
en.B: then the floodwaters would have carried us off, a torrent would have rushed over us,
en.R: Then the flood would have washed us away. The rushing water would have covered us.

fr.L: alors les eaux nous auraient submergés, un torrent aurait passé sur notre âme,
fr.B: alors les eaux en crue nous auraient emportés, un torrent nous aurait recouverts,
fr.R: Alors l’inondation nous aurait emportés. L’eau rapide nous aurait recouverts.

sw.L: basi maji yangetugharikisha, mto wa mafuriko ungepita juu ya nafsi yetu,
sw.B: basi mafuriko yangetuchukua, mkondo wa maji ungetupita juu,
sw.R: Mafuriko yangetusomba. Maji yanayokimbia kwa nguvu yangetufunika.

es.L: entonces las aguas nos habrían arrastrado, un torrente habría pasado sobre nuestra alma;
es.B: entonces la inundación nos habría arrastrado, un torrente nos habría pasado por encima;
es.R: Entonces la inundación nos habría arrastrado. El agua que corría nos habría cubierto.

decisions.choice: torrent: a flash flood in a dry valley
decisions.reason: The word (nachal) is a stream bed, often dry, that fills suddenly with a violent flood after rain. Floods are a common picture of overwhelming enemies (18:5, 17; 69:2-3).

decisions.choice: our soul: us, or our throat
alternatives: our necks (water up to the neck)
decisions.reason: Nefesh is the whole living person, but it can also mean the throat; the water rising over it is drowning (69:2; Jonah 2:6).

decisions.choice: our soul (L); us (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

records.literal_gloss: then would have passed over our soul the waters, the raging [ones].

en.L: then over our soul would have passed the raging waters.
en.B: then the raging waters would have closed over us.
en.R: Those wild waters would have drowned us.

fr.L: alors sur notre âme auraient passé les eaux impétueuses.
fr.B: alors les eaux déchaînées se seraient refermées sur nous.
fr.R: Ces eaux sauvages nous auraient noyés.

sw.L: basi yangepita juu ya nafsi yetu maji yanayochafuka.

es.L: entonces sobre nuestra alma habrían pasado las aguas embravecidas.
es.B: entonces las aguas embravecidas se habrían cerrado sobre nosotros.
es.R: Aquellas aguas salvajes nos habrían ahogado.

decisions.choice: raging: proud, insolent
decisions.reason: The word (zedonim) comes from a root meaning to boil up and to act with arrogance. The waters are pictured like the proud enemies they stand for.

decisions.choice: our soul (L); us (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

decisions.choice: drowned us
decisions.reason: Readable says what the waters going over the throat means (124:4 m2).

source.text: בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֑ה שֶׁלֹּ֥א נְתָנָ֥נוּ טֶ֝֗רֶף לְשִׁנֵּיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be] YHWH, who not has given us [as] prey to their teeth.

en.L: Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who has not given us [as] prey to their teeth.
en.B: Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! He did not give us up to be torn apart by their teeth.
en.R: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}! He did not let our enemies tear us to pieces like wild animals.

fr.L: Béni [soit] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui ne nous a pas donnés [en] proie à leurs dents !
fr.B: Béni soit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Il ne nous a pas livrés pour être déchirés par leurs dents.
fr.R: Louez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ! Il n’a pas laissé nos ennemis nous mettre en pièces comme des bêtes sauvages.

sw.L: Na abarikiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ambaye hakututoa [kuwa] mawindo kwa meno yao.
sw.B: Abarikiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Hakututoa tuchanwe kwa meno yao.
sw.R: Asifiwe {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}! Hakuwaacha adui zetu watupasue vipande vipande kama wanyama wa porini.

es.L: Bendito [sea] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que no nos ha dado [como] presa a sus dientes.
es.B: ¡Bendito sea {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! Él no nos entregó para que sus dientes nos despedazaran.
es.R: ¡Alabado sea {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}! Él no dejó que nuestros enemigos nos hicieran pedazos como animales salvajes.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised
decisions.reason: To bless (barak) the LORD is to praise him with thanks for what he has done.

decisions.choice: prey to their teeth: torn like a hunted animal
decisions.reason: The enemies are now pictured as wild beasts tearing their prey (7:3; 57:5).

decisions.choice: our enemies ... like wild animals
decisions.reason: Readable names the enemies and says what the picture is (m2).

decisions.choice: "abarikiwe" (may he be blessed) at Literal and Balanced; "Asifiwe" (may he be praised) at Readable
decisions.reason: People bless God by speaking well of him with thanks. Literal and Balanced keep the word "bless" (kubariki), as the terms for these psalms do; Readable says "praise", as the English Readable does.

source.text: נַפְשֵׁ֗נוּ כְּצִפּ֥וֹר נִמְלְטָה֮ מִפַּ֪ח י֫וֹקְשִׁ֥ים הַפַּ֥ח נִשְׁבָּ֗ר וַאֲנַ֥חְנוּ נִמְלָֽטְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Our soul like a bird has escaped from [the] snare of fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped.

en.L: Our soul has escaped like a bird from the snare of the fowlers; the snare is broken, and we have escaped.
en.B: We have slipped free like a bird from the bird-catchers' trap; the trap is broken, and we are free!
en.R: We got away like a bird that escapes from a hunter's trap. The trap broke, and we got away!

fr.L: Notre âme s’est échappée comme un oiseau du piège des oiseleurs ; le piège s’est brisé, et nous nous sommes échappés.
fr.B: Nous nous sommes échappés comme un oiseau du filet des chasseurs ; le filet s’est rompu, et nous voilà libres !
fr.R: Nous nous sommes sauvés comme un oiseau qui s’échappe du piège d’un chasseur. Le piège s’est cassé, et nous nous sommes sauvés !

sw.L: Nafsi yetu imeponyoka kama ndege kutoka mtego wa wategaji; mtego umevunjika, nasi tumeponyoka.
sw.B: Tumejinasua kama ndege kutoka kwenye mtego wa wanaonasa ndege; mtego umevunjika, nasi tuko huru!
sw.R: Tuliponyoka kama ndege anayetoroka mtego wa mwindaji. Mtego ulivunjika, nasi tukaponyoka!

es.L: Nuestra alma ha escapado como un pájaro de la trampa de los cazadores; la trampa se ha roto, y nosotros hemos escapado.
es.B: Nos hemos soltado como un pájaro de la trampa de los cazadores de aves; ¡la trampa se rompió, y estamos libres!
es.R: Escapamos como un pájaro que se escapa de la trampa de un cazador. ¡La trampa se rompió, y escapamos!

decisions.choice: the snare of fowlers: a bird trap
decisions.reason: Bird-catchers used nets and spring traps (Amos 3:5; Proverbs 7:23). A bird caught in one could not free itself.

decisions.choice: is broken: broken by someone else
decisions.reason: The verb is passive and does not name who broke the trap; the bird could not, and verses 6 and 8 give the credit to the LORD.

decisions.choice: our soul (L); we (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

source.text: עֶ֭זְרֵנוּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה עֹ֝שֵׂ֗ה שָׁמַ֥יִם וָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Our help [is] in [the] name of YHWH, maker of heaven and earth.

en.L: Our help [is] in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, maker of heaven and earth.
en.B: We find our help in the name of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one who made heaven and earth.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, who made heaven and earth, is the one who helps us.

fr.L: Notre secours [est] dans le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, qui a fait le ciel et la terre.
fr.B: Notre secours, nous le trouvons dans le nom {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, celui qui a fait le ciel et la terre.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui a fait le ciel et la terre, est celui qui nous aide.

sw.L: Msaada wetu [uko] katika jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, muumba wa mbingu na nchi.
sw.B: Tunapata msaada wetu katika jina la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliyeumba mbingu na nchi.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, aliyeumba mbingu na dunia, ndiye anayetusaidia.

es.L: Nuestra ayuda [está] en el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, hacedor de los cielos y de la tierra.
es.B: Encontramos nuestra ayuda en el nombre {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, el que hizo los cielos y la tierra.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, que hizo los cielos y la tierra, es quien nos ayuda.

decisions.choice: the name of the LORD: the LORD himself
decisions.reason: As in 122:4, the name stands for the LORD as he has made himself known, the one his people call on (20:2, 8).

decisions.choice: maker of heaven and earth: the creator of all
decisions.reason: As in 121:2, a title naming the LORD as the creator of everything; it also closes 134:3.

decisions.choice: the LORD ... is the one who helps us
alternatives: in the name of the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of "the name" (m1).
